transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Redwood SE), Martin (Bluehaven VP Eng), Lina (Head of ML), Samir (SRE)

Summary section (auto):
Priya: Quick recap, handoff from sales, we wanna make sure the pilot runway is clear, um, and that network is sorted.

[00:00] Priya: All right, hi everyone. Thanks for making time. This is the onramp strategy and ops handoff for Bluehaven. I'm Priya from Redwood CS, and Ethan's here from SE. Martin, Lina, Samir, thanks for joining.
[00:18] Martin: Yeah thanks, Priya. Appreciate it. Quick note, we had a lot of exec-level interest so wanna make sure we don't slow the pilot.
[00:27] Ethan: Totally understood. Today we'll cover success criteria, which variant to pilot, network setup for either Redwood Private or Dedicated, and the initial benchmark plan.
[00:40] Lina: Sounds good. We're primarily interested in near real-time routing for customer support summarization, so p50 and p95 matter to us, p99 is important but maybe slightly lower priority.
[00:53] Priya: Good, that's helpful. Can you share rough numbers for expected concurrency?
[00:58] Martin: For the pilot, peak concurrency about 60 simultaneous agents, average throughput maybe 200 requests per minute, each request about 200 tokens.
[01:12] Ethan: Okay that maps to the Dedicated pool profile we've seen; we can size a small reserved pool to hit those p95 targets with room to burst. Alternatively, hosted is cheaper but latency variability might be higher.
[01:29] Samir: Quick Q on network — we prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink? Which one does Redwood support for Private deploys?
[01:39] Ethan: We support VPC peering and an S2S VPN for on-prem. For our Redwood Privat (note: transcriber dropped 'e') option there's a customer-managed control plane; we'll send the network checklist. There might be some small NAT traversal steps for logs.
[01:58] Lina: And is customer data at rest encrypted with customer KMS? Our security team needs that.
[02:05] Priya: Yes — KMS integration is available for Private and Dedicated, and we can share SOC2 artifacts. We'll attach security docs in the follow-up.
[02:18] Martin: Great. Also curious about caching — can we persist KV cache between calls, or is that only per-session?
[02:27] Ethan: We have prefix and KV caching options. For the pilot, we can enable prefix cache to reduce token cost on repeated prompts. There is also a KV cache that persists within a session; long-lived persistent KV store is on our roadmap but we can emulate via a low-latency DB if needed.
[02:46] Samir: That emulation detail helps. We'll probably want to control caching TTLs.

[03:10] Ethan: Walkthrough of proposed timeline: week 1 — network & sample data, week 2 — dedicated pool provision + internal smoke tests, week 3 — pilot with 10% production traffic, week 4 — ramp to 100% if quality and latency checks pass.
[03:28] Priya: Success criteria recap: p95 below 400ms for the smaller prompts, p99 below 900ms ideally, correctness metrics: F1 > 0.85 on our labeled prompt set, and no data retention flags. Anyone want to adjust those?
[03:44] Lina: F1 goal is fine. We'll give you the labeled set — top 50 intents to start.
[03:49] Martin: On the p99, if Dedicated hits 700ms we're happy. Hosted would be okay if costs are significantly lower but we want predictability.

[04:10] Speaker 1 (transcription glitch): Uh so about logging, where does the logs land?
[04:15] Ethan: Logs can go to your S3 or to our observability; we usually recommend customer-managed S3 for audit needs. We'll provide access controls and token-level breakdowns in the Console. (note: sometimes shows 'Redwood Counsle' in auto notes)
[04:33] Samir: We need also to know egress IPs and the firewall ranges to open.
[04:37] Priya: We'll include the egress list in the network checklist. Samir, can you confirm your team's maintenance windows for peering?
[04:45] Samir: We operate 08:00–18:00 weekdays; prefer peering in off-peak, so we'll target next Tuesday night.

[05:10] Martin: One blocker I can think of is compliance sign-off — our legal wants an updated DPA and assurance around data residency as some EU data may be involved later.
[05:20] Priya: Understood, we'll attach the DPA and our compliance pack; for data residency we can region-lock models and storage in the EU region when that scope arrives.

[06:05] Ethan: On tooling for monitoring: we'll set up the Redwood Console dashboards for you, with token-level cost, latency histograms, and error traces. We'll also create an alerts policy — e.g., p95>500ms triggers Slack alert to your ops channel.
[06:22] Lina: Can we also get model-quality alerts? Like regression on classification accuracy per prompt set?
[06:29] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize has eval hooks; we'll wire your labeled prompts into the quality monitoring. There might be an extra config step to map prompt IDs.

[07:00] Priya: Ok, let's do a short risk register — main risks: network delay to provision peering, slower-than-expected latency in Hosted option, model regressions on edge cases. Mitigations: dedicated pool, smoke tests, and rollback to previous model version.
[07:18] Martin: Sounds reasonable. Also cost — we may want to run dual-mode for a week to compare unit cost under load.
[07:25] Ethan: We can enable cost tracing per request so you can attribute token spend to features.

[08:40] Priya: Next steps recap: we'll send the onramp playbook, security docs, and the network checklist; Ethan will provision a small Dedicated trial and run initial benchmarks; Bluehaven will send the sample prompt set and a labeled subset for quality evaluation.
[09:00] Lina: We'll prepare the prompts and a small labeled set (50 intents) and aim to send by Friday.
[09:10] Samir: I'll confirm firewall rules and peering window by Thursday.
[09:18] Martin: Can we schedule the network walkthrough with Ethan? Prefer next Tuesday 20:00 PT.
[09:23] Ethan: I can do that, yes.

[09:50] Priya: Any other concerns?
[09:55] Martin: Only that we need the pricing snapshot for Dedicated vs Hosted for the pilot scale — that will help exec approval.
[10:03] Priya: I'll include a simplified pricing sheet in the follow up, plus an estimate of run-rate at projected traffic.

[10:30] Ethan: One small technical note — if you plan long sequences, we recommend the quantized model variant to keep GPU memory small; the cost tradeoff is negligible for your pilot but helps at higher concurrency.
[10:46] Lina: Good to know, we'll flag sequences above 2k tokens separately.

[11:10] Priya: Ok I'll send the follow-up email with attachments and assign owners on action items. Thanks everyone.
[11:18] Martin: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:22] Lina: Thanks.
[11:25] Samir: Bye.

(auto notes): Links shared: onramp-playbook.docx (Priya), sample-prompt-template.csv (Lina), dedicated-trial-access-invite (Ethan).
